title: Approval rule configuration identifies its eligible decision-maker
question: Compare the isolated eligibility declaration check with the complete Requirement identity, subject and current-outcome obligations; do not infer a Decision-history evaluator from configuration validation.

evidence.title: Approver configuration validation does not establish a complete Approval Requirement
explanation: AuthorizationRule.validate_rule rejects a configuration without an approving user or role and rejects selected maker/checker identity overlap and unsupported product-discount configurations. The method checks a bounded approval-rule configuration, not committed Approval Decisions or their current effectiveness.

The selected declaration-rejection cases map one eligible actor to approving_user and absent/null eligibility to an absent native approver. Other native policy fields are explicitly unset; the method itself does not check a FinKore Requirement identifier or subject association. Returning normally is a successful validation call, not an inferred PENDING or APPROVED result.

On 2026-11-23, the exact pinned validate_rule AST was executed in isolation with Python 3.10.12. Translation and framework throw were dependency doubles; the throw facade raised a validation exception, and any unexpected numeric helper call failed rather than providing a financial substitute. Frappe Document lifecycle, database validation, permissions, role resolution, discount arithmetic and Decision history were not executed. Checks in surrounding layers may differ; no whole-ERPNext or full Approval implementation claim follows.

historical_publications.title: ERPNext — Approver configuration checks
explanation: The isolated native validator rejected a missing approving user or role. This configuration observation provides context for explicit eligibility; it did not evaluate a Requirement state, Decision history or the complete Core Requirement contract. No comparable Approvals conformance score is published.

Exact-method isolation with framework translation/throw doubles and explicitly unset unrelated product-policy fields. The native method is not a complete Requirement evaluator. No Frappe lifecycle/database behavior, eligible-role expansion, committed Decisions, expiration, withdrawal, supersession or approval-chain evaluation is established.
